aspects.says: javac checks that a container has a value() array of the repeatable type, a retention at least as long and no extra targets.
basis: section:A Repeated Annotation Is Stored Inside Its Container
aspects.reason: a rule javac enforces has no wrong solution that compiles, so no graded test can tell a right container from a wrong one; the page shows the compile error

aspects.says: A default is stored in the annotation type and filled in when the annotation is read, so changing it changes what callers compiled earlier read.
basis: section:Defaults Live in the Annotation Type, and Only value Can Go Unnamed

aspects.says: An annotation element is a primitive, String, Class, enum, annotation or a one-dimensional array of these, and every value, defaults included, is a compile-time constant, so null, collections and values computed at run time are refused by javac.
basis: section:An Element Holds a Compile-Time Constant of a Few Types

aspects.says: @Inherited makes getAnnotation find a class annotation on the nearest superclass, never on an interface, a method or for an annotation without @Inherited.
basis: section:@Inherited Reaches a Class Only from Its Superclasses

aspects.says: An annotation written more than once is stored inside its container, so getAnnotation finds either the single annotation or the container, and getAnnotationsByType finds every one.
basis: section:A Repeated Annotation Is Stored Inside Its Container

aspects.says: javac refuses an annotation used where its @Target doesn't allow it; without @Target it is allowed on every declaration and in no type context.
basis: section:@Target Is Checked by javac at Every Use

aspects.says: Only an element named value can be written without its name, and only when every other element has a default.
basis: section:Defaults Live in the Annotation Type, and Only value Can Go Unnamed
